Apple is up 25% in the past year. The companies that supply Apple are up 135%.

Goldman's basket of US Apple suppliers has returned roughly 135% since last October, more than five times Apple's 25%. The brand that sells the iPhone badly lagged the companies that build it.

This is the AI-hardware trade in one chart. The gains are in the picks and shovels, the chips, optics and assembly inside the device, far more than in the brand stamped on it. When a supply chain outruns its marquee customer this badly, the market is telling you where the real demand sits.

$AAPL

SpaceX has round-tripped its entire IPO in four months.

The stock popped 49% out of the gate, then crashed 46% to below its $130 IPO price by August, and has now ripped 48% off that bottom. The latest leg is a $750 billion rally that pushed it back above the IPO price and put Elon Musk back in trillionaire territory.

Nothing about the business changed 90% in four months. The sentiment did. A brand-new mega-cap with a huge story and no public track record trades on narrative, and narrative cuts both ways. Respect the round trip.

$SPCX

tweets.text:
Europe tried to wall out Chinese cars with EV tariffs. Chinese brands just took one in four hybrid sales instead.

Chinese automakers like BYD now hold 25% of Europe's hybrid market, a record, plus about one in three plug-in hybrid sales. That pushed their share of all European new-car sales to a record 12%.

The EU's tariffs were aimed at electric vehicles, so Chinese makers routed the same volume through hybrids, which those tariffs barely touch. Brussels is now moving to close that gap too. Tariffs redirect a flow, they rarely stop it, and the next workaround is already on the table.

tweets.text:
High rates are supposed to kill capital spending. This cycle, they are not even slowing it.

Real capital spending keeps climbing while the cost of capital sits at a two-decade high. The forward signal is louder: new orders for core capital goods, which lead real capex by about three months, just snapped back toward +14% year over year.

The textbook says expensive money throttles investment first. The AI and power buildout does not read the textbook. It runs on its own fuel, which means the Fed's biggest lever has lost its grip on the part of the economy that is actually growing. No rate cut is what powers this, and no rate hike is what stops it.

tweets.text:
Canada just shed another 68,300 jobs in a single month.

September's drop dragged total third-quarter job losses to about 35,000 net, with the damage led by the public sector. The Canadian labor market is now visibly cracking.

Canada is the canary for a rate-squeezed consumer. Mortgages reset every few years there instead of being locked for 30, household debt is among the highest in the developed world, and the job market is the first thing to give. Watch it as a live preview of what high rates eventually do to an over-levered economy.
